commits.author: Aman Riat
commits.message:
Fix FOSSA scan: scan repository root instead of per-module paths (#213)

* Scan repository root for FOSSA instead of per-module paths

The matrix-based scan produced no results in FOSSA. Each matrix entry ran
`fossa analyze --only-path <child-module>`, but the FOSSA Maven strategy
discovers a single project at the root reactor pom. Filtering discovery to a
child module directory excluded that root project, so the maven project was
skipped and zero dependencies were uploaded.

Both matrix entries also passed the identical
`--project SolaceProducts_solace-spring-boot --revision <sha>`, so they raced
to write the same FOSSA locator regardless.

Collapse to a single root scan and add a root .fossa.yml. Verified locally:
the root scan resolves 84 Maven dependencies where --only-path resolved 0.

update_manifest is collapsed to one entry named after the repository, matching
the product name the Guardian upload already derives from the FOSSA project ID.

* Run the SCA scan on pull requests as well as pushes to master

Lets the root-scan fix be validated on the PR itself instead of only after
merge. The reusable workflow already handles PR context: it scans in diff mode,
posts a PR comment and status check, and uploads under branch 'PR'.

update_manifest stays master-only -- its existing
`github.ref_name == github.event.repository.default_branch` guard is false on
pull_request events, so no DynamoDB writes happen from PRs.

* Give the FOSSA scan Maven credentials for GitHub Packages

The root scan uploaded real data but the dependency graph was shallow:
23 dependencies for spring-cloud where a local run with a warm ~/.m2 resolves 92.
`fossa analyze --debug` showed why:

    Warn: Could not analyze edges between dependencies.
    Warn: Could not analyze deep dependencies.
    [ERROR] Non-resolvable import POM: com.solace.test.integration:
            solace-integration-test-support-bom:pom:3.0.0 (absent):
            Could not find artifact ... in central

That BOM is published to GitHub Packages, not Maven Central. build-test.yml
resolves it with `mvn -s maven/settings.xml` plus GITHUB_TOKEN, but the FOSSA
CLI shells out to a plain `mvn` that never sees that file, so the import POM
fails, dependency:tree errors out, and FOSSA degrades to a graph with no
transitive edges -- silently, as a warning rather than a failure.

Configure the same repository and credentials into ~/.m2/settings.xml via the
reusable workflow's maven-settings setup action, which plain `mvn` picks up.

* Use github.token instead of secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN in the reusable call

The secrets context is not available in jobs.<id>.with for a reusable workflow
call, so the workflow failed validation before any job started. github.token
carries the same value and is an allowed context there.

* Set up Java before writing Maven settings

maven-settings-xml-action failed with "Cannot read properties of undefined
(reading 'nodeType')" because it was run without setup-java, so there was no
~/.m2 settings.xml for it to build on. Restore setup-java alongside it and pin
JDK 17 / zulu to match build-test.yml.

* Revert the Maven-credentials attempt for the FOSSA scan

The shallow-dependency-graph problem is real but cannot be fixed from the
caller side. Two blockers:

  1. github.token (and secrets.*) resolve to an empty string when passed
     through a reusable workflow's `with:` block, so the server password
     arrived empty:
       servers: [{"id": "...", "username": "AmanRiat1", "password": ""}]
  2. maven-settings-xml-action then failed outright:
       invalid doc source @#[line:0,col:undefined]
       ##[error]Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'nodeType')

Revert to the known-good root-scan configuration, which is green and uploads
real results. The remaining transitive-depth gap needs either a credential
secret plumbed through sca-scan-and-guard.yaml or a Vault-sourced
packages-read token; tracked separately.

* Install the test-support BOM so FOSSA resolves transitive dependencies

The root scan uploaded real data but a shallow graph: 18 dependencies where a
local run with a warm ~/.m2 resolves 84. The root pom imports
com.solace.test.integration:solace-integration-test-support-bom:3.0.0, which is
not on Maven Central. The FOSSA CLI shells out to a plain `mvn`, the import POM
fails to resolve, dependency:tree errors, and FOSSA degrades to a graph with no
transitive edges -- as a warning, not a failure.

No credentials are required. build-test.yml already handles this by cloning the
public SolaceDev/solace-integration-test-support repo at the tag named by
solace.integration.test.support.version and running `mvn install`. Do the same
in custom_setup_script, cloning to RUNNER_TEMP so FOSSA does not pick the clone
up as a separate project to scan.

This supersedes the reverted attempt to authenticate against GitHub Packages,
which could not work: github.token is emptied when passed through a reusable
workflow's `with:` block.
